description: Parent-source data for 36 webapp parcel-story slots and the provisional A1/A2/B/C working parcel model. Editorial slots are not historic tithe plot numbers. The timeline also preserves unresolved research leads about the Thomas estate/probate and John Williams’s unknown death date.

map_reference.image_role: Photograph of a tithe schedule page, not a geographic map or selected parcel polygon
map_reference.overlay_status: No historic polygon is highlighted until the exact row and boundary are verified

parcel_model.label: Parcel A — north woods plus house and garden
parcel_model.description: Current working model: Parcel A comprises A1 (the north woods) and A2 (the house, buildings and garden). The green south of the house is outside Parcel A. The 1928 family understanding of freehold is a testimony-based interpretation to test against the 1877 arrangement and Thomas estate/probate records.
parcel_model.limits: Analytical reconstruction, not yet a surveyed boundary. The 1877 instrument and plan remain essential to confirming extent and title.

parcel_model.label: A1 — north woods
parcel_model.description: The current model places the woods north of Mary Williams’s house within Parcel A as A1. The family/working account associates this ground with a 1955 taking, but the original order, writ, execution return and 1961 woodland deed must be compared before fixing the legal or physical extent.
parcel_model.limits: Do not assume that the wording “whole farm” proves that the order included A1; distinguish the order’s target from what was physically taken.

parcel_model.label: A2 — house, buildings and garden
parcel_model.description: The farmhouse, buildings and garden are analysed as A2, the house part of Parcel A. The family’s reported 1928 freehold understanding and the later separate registration of the farmhouse are central to the current theory.
parcel_model.limits: The exact instrument, boundary, legal effect of the 1928 event and the relevant 1982–83 registration file remain to be verified. Alfred Thomas’s death is dated 14 December 1927 by biography, but the reported Cardiff Corporation bequest is only a secondary transcription; the will has not been inspected.

parcel_model.label: Parcel B — eastern/right-hand fields
parcel_model.description: The current interpretation treats Parcel B as the eastern/right-hand agricultural fields covered by the 1939 WGR–John Williams tenancy plan and as the intended subject of the 1955 Order 14 action.
parcel_model.limits: The later phrase “whole farm” is ambiguous in this reconstruction. The original order and execution return are needed to establish its extent and what was taken. The allegation that the 1939 agreement was fraudulent remains unproven.

parcel_model.label: Parcel C — green south of the house
parcel_model.description: The green south of Mary Williams’s house is treated as a separate parcel, Parcel C, outside Parcel A. The possibility that Williams held title or a possessory interest in C is an open question, not an established fact.
parcel_model.limits: Check the village-green VG41 application and map, the 1955 writ/return and relevant conveyances. Do not fold C back into Parcel A.

model_events.title: North woods and the 1955 taking
model_events.details: The current working account places the north woods in A1 and associates them with a 1955 taking. At the same time, the working interpretation treats Order 14 as directed at Parcel B. The original order, writ, execution return and 1961 woodland deed must resolve how the wording, intended parcel and physical taking relate.
model_events.status: Working account; primary execution record required

model_events.title: Alfred Thomas dies; reported Cardiff Corporation bequest requires probate verification
model_events.details: The Dictionary of Welsh Biography dates Alfred Thomas, 1st Baron Pontypridd’s death to 14 December 1927. A secondary transcription of a 27 December 1927 report described a bequest of most of his property to Cardiff Corporation, but its original newspaper has not been identified and the will has not been inspected. Nothing located so far establishes that the estate included the Llandough house parcel. A grant reportedly made in 1928 and the contents of the will remain to be checked.
model_events.status: Death date supported by biography; bequest is a secondary report not yet confirmed; land effect unknown

model_events.title: Reported end of rent and asserted freehold transition
model_events.details: Mary Williams’s later account places the last rent payment to Alfred Thomas in 1928. The current theory is that the Williams family then understood the freehold of Parcel A to have passed to them. The deed, receipt and exact boundary have not been established; this is family testimony plus inference, not a registry finding. The relationship between the date of death in 1927, any executor or estate, and the reported 1928 rent payment needs primary documentation.
model_events.status: Family testimony; instrument and probate context not yet established

model_events.title: John Williams’s death date must be established before linking it to the 1949–52 sequence
model_events.details: The current John Williams research page records that he was still alive and very ill in the early 1950s, but his date of death has not been established and a death certificate has not yet been obtained. Mary’s later account places her continued occupation after his death. The possibility that the timing of his death relates to the 1949 surrender/regrant, missing papers around 1950–52, or later possession steps is a research hypothesis until the death record and underlying documents are checked.
model_events.status: Death date unknown; do not infer a connection from proximity alone

model_events.title: WGR–John Williams tenancy plan depicts the fields
model_events.details: The extant research catalogue describes the 1939 plan as depicting the eastern fields (working Parcel B) and not the house parcel. The user’s hypothesis is that the agreement may have been used to recast occupation as permissive and could have been fraudulent; that allegation must be tested against the original agreement, plan and surrounding correspondence.
model_events.status: Plan described in the catalogue; authenticity and legal effect remain to be tested

model_events.title: Surrender and re-grant of the agricultural tenancy
model_events.details: The later Court of Appeal account describes John Williams’s agricultural tenancy as surrendered and a new yearly tenancy for Frederick beginning on 2 February 1949. Read against the 1939 plan, the current working interpretation places this transaction on Parcel B. Whether this was part of a coordinated strategy affecting the separate house parcel is not established by the date or transaction alone.
model_events.status: Court-history lead; original instrument and exact extent remain to be checked

model_events.title: Missing title papers and the later letting decision
model_events.details: Mary’s account reports that title or farm papers went missing from a blanket box around this period; a lodger was said to have taken them at Mr Knapp’s request, which is uncorroborated testimony. The later court history records agents deciding not to proceed with Frederick’s letting in 1952. The underlying papers and any written termination notice have not been inspected, so the exact sequence and causal relationship remain open.
model_events.status: Family account and later court history; primary papers required

model_events.date_text: May 1951 (12 years after May 1939; arithmetic only)
model_events.title: Test the proposed 12-year trigger against the actual tenancy documents
model_events.details: The calendar interval from the May 1939 agreement reaches twelve years in May 1951. The hypothesis is that WGR used this point to end or decline to renew an arrangement and then pursue possession. No termination document establishing that trigger has been inspected here; the later 1952 letting decision is near enough to investigate but does not prove the theory.
model_events.status: Date arithmetic only; no demonstrated causal link

model_events.title: Order 14 and the phrase “whole farm”
model_events.details: The current working interpretation is that the order was directed at Parcel B, the eastern/right-hand fields. Its later-described “whole farm” wording must not be treated as proof that Parcel A was included. The original order and execution return are needed to establish both its legal scope and the ground physically taken; the separate reasons given for leaving the house and garden undisturbed must not replace Mary’s asserted ownership.
model_events.status: Interpretation under test; original order and execution return required

model_events.title: Green south of the house registered as VG41
model_events.details: The green is treated in the current parcel model as separate Parcel C, not part of Parcel A. Whether Williams held title or a possessory interest in C remains open. The VG41 application, map, notice and objection file is needed to determine what was registered and on what basis.
model_events.status: Registration date recited; underlying application file not yet inspected
